newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexico crude ports shut amid strong winds.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexico crude ports shut amid strong winds.

text.p: Two Gulf of Mexico crude shipping ports were reported closed on Friday as wind speeds escalated in the region, port authorities told Reuters.

Pajaritos in Veracruz was closed at 1405 local/2005 GMT, after reopening on 0600 local/1200 GMT Friday. Dos Bocas in Tabasco state shut at 1350 local/1950 GMT because of strong winds, a port official said.
At Pajaritos and Dos Bocas winds were reported between 55 and 65 km per hour with waves six to eight feet high. .
The Communications and Transport Ministry reported a total of five Gulf of Mexico ports shut as a cold front headed southwest through the region.
The third of state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos' (Pemex) crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, was reported open with winds up to 30 km per hour.
Cayo Arcas ships an average 611,000 barrels per day (bpd), Dos Bocas exports about 440,000 bpd and Pajaritos ships about 399,000 bpd, according to the latest Pemex figures.
